title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $5.53 sold 2 and 4 units (below baseline 4.0). Easter week (2026-03-30) sold 6 at same price, but was an event. No other data confirms price elasticity. Noise-adjusted promotion lifts are x1.0. Price increase likely dampens demand.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 4.0. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 5.1% to $5.53. Past promotions show median uplift x1.54, but noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0—indicating no reliable lift. The week after a promotion typically sees x0.84, but noise-adjusted is x1.0. Recent weeks at $5.53 show low sales (2, 4), suggesting price sensitivity. Easter week (2026-03-30) sold 6 units at $5.53, vs baseline 4.0—x1.5 uplift, but no event. This week’s price is identical to that of Easter, but no holiday. Evidence is thin: one past Easter week at same price, but no other signals. Shrink toward 1.0. Final adjustment: slight downside risk from price hike.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-26 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.53 (+5.1% vs regular price 5.26)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 4.0 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-98% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
